cards.title: The basic equation
cards.html:
Every sale is split into three parts:

Sales = VC + FC + Profit
└ VC + FC = TC (total cost)
  • VC — variable cost: changes with the units sold.
  • FC — fixed cost: stays the same whatever the sales.
  • TC — total cost = VC + FC.
  • So Profit = Sales − TC.

Everything in this chapter — contribution, P/V ratio, break-even point, margin of safety, desired sales and the income statement — comes out of this one equation.

cards.title: Contribution
cards.html:
Contribution is what is left from sales after paying the variable cost. It first covers the fixed cost; the balance is profit.

Sales = VC + FC + Profit
Cont= Sales − VC
Cont= FC + Profit
Cont % = 100 − VC %

Special cases

  • Where the business does not earn profit (no profit no loss): Cont = FC
  • Where the business is making a loss: Cont = FC − Loss

cards.q: Q1. Calculate contribution in each of the following independent situations: (i) Fixed cost Rs. 8,000, profit Rs. 5,600 (ii) Variable cost Rs. 7,000, sales Rs. 11,000.
cards.a:
(i) Cont = FC + Profit
= 8,000 + 5,600
= 13,600
(ii) Cont = Sales − VC
= 11,000 − 7,000
= 4,000

cards.q: Q2. Calculate P/V ratio in each of the following independent situations: (i) Variable cost Rs. 60, Contribution Rs. 40 (ii) Sales Rs. 20, variable cost Rs. 15 (iii) Ratio of variable cost to sales 84% (iv) Profit Rs. 5,000; Sales Rs. 25,000; Fixed cost Rs. 8,000 (v) Year I Sales Rs. 50,000, Total cost Rs. 40,000; Year II Sales Rs. 60,000, Total cost Rs. 45,000.
cards.a:
(i) VC = 60, Cont = 40
Sales = VC + FC + Profit (FC + Profit = Cont)
Sales = 60 + 40 = 100
PVR = Cont ÷ Sales × 100 = 40 ÷ 100 × 100 = 40%
(ii) Cont = Sales − VC = 20 − 15 = 5
PVR = 5 ÷ 20 × 100 = 25%
(iii) PVR = 100 − VC %
= 100 − 84
= 16%
(iv) PVR = Cont ÷ Sales × 100
Cont = 5,000 + 8,000 = 13,000
PVR = 13,000 ÷ 25,000 × 100 = 52%
(v)SalesTCProfit
Year I50,00040,00050,000 − 40,000 = 10,000
Year II60,00045,00060,000 − 45,000 = 15,000
Δ in profit = 15,000 − 10,000 = 5,000
Δ in sales = 60k − 50k = 10,000
PVR = Δ in Profit ÷ Δ in Sales × 100 = 5,000 ÷ 10,000 × 100 = 50%

cards.q: Q3 (class work — PVR). Following data is given: Total fixed cost = Rs. 12,000; Selling price = Rs. 12 per unit; Variable cost = Rs. 9 per unit. Calculate the P/V ratio.
cards.a:
CPU = 12 − 9 = 3
PVR = CPU ÷ SPU × 100
= 3 ÷ 12 × 100 = 25%

cards.q: What is contribution? Write its formulas, including the no-profit-no-loss and loss cases.
cards.a:
Contribution is sales minus variable cost; it covers fixed cost and the balance is profit.

  • Cont = Sales − VC
  • Cont = FC + Profit
  • Cont % = 100 − VC %
  • No profit no loss: Cont = FC
  • Loss: Cont = FC − Loss

cards.q: Write the five formulas of the P/V ratio.
cards.a:
1. Cont (₹) ÷ Sales × 100
  2. Cont %
  3. 100 − VC %
  4. Cont per unit ÷ Sales per unit × 100
  5. Change in profit ÷ Change in sales × 100 (when two years' total cost and sales are given)

cards.title: Break Even Point — meaning
cards.html:
Break-even point is the level of sales at which there is no profit or no loss: contribution exactly equals fixed cost.

Sales = VC + FC
Sales = TC

It can be shown by a chart or found by a formula.

Class example

Sales = 2,000; VC = 1,200 (60%); FC = 800
At BEPSales fall
Sales2,0001,800
(−) VC1,2001,080
Cont800720
(−) FC800800
Profit0(80) Loss

At sales of 2,000 the contribution (800) just covers the fixed cost (800). When sales fall to 1,800, VC falls with it (60%), contribution drops to 720 and there is a loss of 80.

cards.title: BEP formulas & desired sales
cards.html:
1. Sales = VC + FC
  2. Sales = TC
  3. BEP (₹) = FC ÷ PVR
  4. BEP (unit) = FC ÷ CPU, where CPU = contribution per unit
Sales = VC + [Profit + FC]
BEP (₹) = BEP (unit) × SP
Desired sales = (FC + Profit) ÷ PVR / CPU

For desired sales the target profit is added to fixed cost: divide by PVR for sales in ₹, by CPU for sales in units.

items.n: CPU = contribution per unit = SP − VC per unit
No profit or no loss; Cont = FC
Sales needed to earn a target profit

cards.title: Changes in SP, VC and FC — effect on BEP
cards.html:
From Q7: change one item at a time and recompute PVR, then BEP = FC ÷ PVR.

Q7 — what happens to BEP?Sales 2,00,000 · VC 1,20,000 · FC 30,000 · PVR 40% · BEP 75,000
  • SP reduced 10%sales 1,80,000, VC same → Cont 60,000 → PVR 33.33% → BEP 90,000
  • VC increases 10%VC 1,32,000 → Cont 68,000 → PVR 34% → BEP 88,235
  • FC increases 10%FC 33,000, PVR still 40% → BEP 82,500

A change in selling price or variable cost changes the PVR; a change in fixed cost leaves PVR the same and changes BEP directly.

cards.title: Units sold drop vs selling price drop
cards.html:
⚑ Looks like a slip: “Sales drop → 10%” is worked as (5,000 − 50) = 4,950 units — 50 is 1% of 5,000; 10% would be 500 (4,500 units).

Sales fall — two different cases5,000 units · SP 5 · VC 3 → sales 25,000, VC 15,000
  • Units sold dropsales and VC both fall (units × SP, units × VC) → 4,950 × 5 = 24,750 · 4,950 × 3 = 14,850
  • Selling price drops 10%SP 5 − 0.5 = 4.5 → sales 4.5 × 5,000 = 22,500 · VC stays 5,000 × 3 = 15,000
Unit 5,000 sold;SP 5;VC 3
→ Sales = 25,000
VC= 15,000
Sales drop → 10%:
Sales (5,000 − 50) = 4,950
Sales = 4,950 × 5 = 24,750
VC = 4,950 × 3 = 14,850
# Selling price 10% decrease:
SP = 5 − 0.5 = 4.5
VC = 3
Sales = 4.5 × 5,000 = 22,500
VC = 5,000 × 3 = 15,000

When fewer units are sold, both sales and variable cost go down. When only the selling price falls, the same units are sold, so variable cost does not change — only sales (and contribution) fall.

cards.q: Q4. The following data is given: Fixed cost = Rs. 12,000 (total); Selling price = Rs. 15 per unit; Variable cost = Rs. 9 per unit. Calculate (a) Profit at a sales level of Rs. 2,10,000 (b) Sales to earn a profit of Rs. 75,000 (c) Break even point in rupees (d) Break even point in units.

(c) BEP (₹) = FC ÷ PVR

BEP = 12,000 ÷ 0.4 = ₹30,000
(d) BEP (unit) = FC ÷ CPU = 12,000 ÷ 6 = 2,000
BEP (₹) = BEP (unit) × SP = 2,000 × 15 = 30,000

cards.q: Q6. Given: Break-even point = Rs. 30,000; Profit = Rs. 1,500; Fixed cost = Rs. 6,000. What is the amount of variable cost?
cards.a:
⚑ Missing in the PDF: Q5 isn't in the notes — they go from Q4 straight to Q6. Was it skipped in class, or is a page missing?

BEP (₹) = FC ÷ PVR
30,000 = 6,000 ÷ PVR
PVR = 6,000 ÷ 30,000 = 20%
Cont = FC + Profit = 6,000 + 1,500 = 7,500
Cont % = PVR %
VC = 100 − PVR = 100 − 20 = 80%
Sales = 7,500 × 100 ÷ 20 = 37,500
VC = 37,500 × 80% = 30,000

(b) New sales = 2,00,000 − 20,000 = 1,80,000
VC 1,20,000
Cont 60,000

(c) Sales = 2,00,000

cards.q: What is the break-even point? Write its formulas.
cards.a:
The level of sales at which there is no profit or no loss (contribution = fixed cost).

  • Sales = VC + FC
  • Sales = TC
  • BEP (₹) = FC ÷ PVR
  • BEP (unit) = FC ÷ CPU
  • BEP (₹) = BEP (unit) × SP

cards.title: Flow charts — Margin of Safety
cards.html:
Actual Sales12,000 (100%)
  • Break-even sales10,000 → no profit no loss
  • Margin of Safety12,000 − 10,000 = 2,000

BEP % + MOS % = 100.

Actual sales 12,000
→
− BEP sales 10,000
→
= MOS 2,000
Margin of Safety (MOS)MOS = AS − BES
  • ① MOS = Actual sales − BEP (₹)
  • ② MOS % = 100 − BEP %
  • ③ MOS = Profit ÷ PVR
  • ④ MOS = Profit ÷ CPU
  • ⑤ MOS (unit) = Actual sales (unit) − BEP (unit)

AS = actual sales, BES = break-even sales.

cards.title: Margin of Safety — meaning
cards.html:
Margin of safety is the sales above the break-even point — how far sales can fall before the business starts making a loss.

MOS = AS − BES
BEP = 10,000 → no profit no loss
Sales 10,000 → profit 0
Actual sales 12,000 − 10,000 = 2,000 → MOS

cards.title: MOS formulas
cards.html:
1. MOS = Actual sales − BEP (₹)
  2. MOS % = 100 − BEP %
  3. MOS = Profit ÷ PVR
  4. MOS = Profit ÷ CPU
  5. MOS (unit) = Actual sales (unit) − BEP (unit)

Turned around (used in Q11 and Q12): BEP % = 100 − MOS %, BEP (₹) = Sales × BEP %, BEP = AS − MOS.

cards.title: Which formula? — MOS and BEP
cards.html:
Find MOS — what is given? (Q10)
  • BEP % & actual salesMOS % = 100 − BEP %, MOS (₹) = Sales × MOS %
  • Actual units & BEP unitsMOS (unit) = AS − BEP
  • BEP % onlyMOS % = 100 − BEP %
  • PVR & profitMOS = Profit ÷ PVR
  • CPU & profitMOS (unit) = Profit ÷ CPU
Find BEP — what is given? (Q12)
  • FC & PVRBEP (₹) = FC ÷ PVR
  • FC & CPUBEP (unit) = FC ÷ CPU
  • MOS % onlyBEP % = 100 − MOS %
  • FC & VC-to-sales ratioCont % = 100 − VC % = PVR, then FC ÷ PVR
  • Actual sales & MOS %BEP % = 100 − MOS %, BEP (₹) = Sales × BEP %
  • Profit, MOS % & VC %MOS ÷ 100 = Profit ÷ PVR → Sales → BEP % → BEP
  • Actual sales & MOS (₹)BEP = AS − MOS (₹)
  • Actual units & MOS unitsBEP = AS (unit) − MOS (unit)

cards.q: Q10. Calculate margin of safety in each of the following independent situations: (i) Break even point 40%, Actual sales Rs. 40,000 (ii) Actual sales – 40,000 units, Break-even point 25,000 units (iii) Break-even point – 75% (iv) P/V ratio 40%, Profit Rs. 35,000 (v) Contribution per unit Rs. 20, Profit Rs. 15,000.
cards.a:
⚑ Unclear in the PDF: In (v) the profit is written “1500” on the board — read as 15,000 (the question says 15,000).

(i) MOS % = 100 − 40% = 60%
MOS (₹) = Sales × MOS %
= 40,000 × 60% = 24,000
(ii) MOS (unit) = AS − BEP
= 40,000 − 25,000
= 15,000 unit
(iii) MOS (%) = 100 − BEP %
= 100 − 75%
= 25%
(iv) MOS = Profit ÷ PVR = 35,000 ÷ 0.4 = 87,500
(v) MOS (unit) = Profit ÷ CPU = 15,000 ÷ 20 = 750

cards.q: Q11. The profit/volume ratio of Escorts Ltd. is 50% and the margin of safety is 40%. You are required to work out the net profit and the break-even point if sales volume is Rs. 10,00,000.
cards.a:
Sales = 10,00,000
BEP % = 100 − MOS %
BEP = 100 − 40% = 60%
BEP (₹) = Sales × BEP %
= 10,00,000 × 60 ÷ 100 = 6,00,000
BEP = FC ÷ PVR
6,00,000 = FC ÷ 0.5
FC = 3,00,000
Net Profit = Cont − FC
Cont = 10,00,000 × 50% = 5L
Profit = 5L − 3L = 2,00,000

(ii) BEP (unit) = FC ÷ CPU = 15,000 ÷ 3 = 5,000

= 100 − 20% = 80%
(iv) BEP (₹) = FC ÷ PVR
Cont % = PVR
Cont % = 100 − VC % = 100 − 60 = 40%
BEP = 9,000 ÷ 0.4 = 22,500
(v) BEP % = 100 − MOS %
= 100 − 30% = 70%
BEP (₹) = Sales × BEP % = 50,000 × 70% = 35,000

cards.q: What is margin of safety? Write its formulas.
cards.a:
The excess of actual sales over break-even sales: MOS = AS − BES.

  • MOS = Actual sales − BEP (₹)
  • MOS % = 100 − BEP %
  • MOS = Profit ÷ PVR
  • MOS = Profit ÷ CPU
  • MOS (unit) = Actual sales (unit) − BEP (unit)
